parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the national passport sex-marker restriction, now in effect after the November 2025 Supreme Court order, creates universal document exposure, with reported passport confiscation and stranding. Entry refusal on any document discrepancy, plus a fraud-based lifetime ineligibility route, adds entry risk. Documented national custody harms include forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse in immigration custody, and birth-sex-based corrections policy. The division adds a school and college facilities designation with no enforcement mechanism and no documented case, and an announced marker-matching rule. Mitigations are real but partial: national hate-crime and employment protection, marriage recognition, and 33 local ordinances. Local criminal bathroom enforcement is not confirmed for this division. The rating is driven by national custody and document practices.

entry_documents.exposure: Passports cannot carry a marker differing from sex at birth; new applications are M or F only. Passports reported confiscated or blocked, with some travellers stranded. Entry refusal on any document discrepancy; fraud-based lifetime ineligibility is possible though not automatic.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry. Litigation is ongoing. No division-level document protection for visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-country documents meeting a US-style marker mismatch at the border, or at federal and state document checks, can escalate to secondary inspection and detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented with forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. A state arrest for trespass in a restroom was documented, with 24 hours in a men's ward. Corrections bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to leave when asked; it is not automatic arrest. No documented court relief in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: National custody practice applies to any visitor who is detained at a federal checkpoint, regardless of division protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law requires K-12 schools and colleges, public and private, to designate facilities by birth-certificate sex, with students required to use matching facilities. Single-occupancy controlled-use rooms exempt. Four states criminalise certain trans bathroom use; this division's status is not confirmed.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No enforcement mechanism and no documented penalty. Facilities designation is not a general government-building ban in the sources.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitors are rarely in these settings; minors in school are the main exposure. Federal and state facilities exposures stack.

care_services.exposure: State bill bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for under-18s, but its enforceability is unresolved after a March 2025 re-injunction. National proposed rules would bar public reimbursement for under-18s. National subpoenas of hospital records for patients under 19.
care_services.protection: Adult care restrictions were withdrawn in February 2024. No documented adult care denial in the division.
care_services.interaction: A minor visitor's care could be disrupted or exposed in records. Adult care is not documented as restricted.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders target gender-affirming care and school facilitators, with prosecution threatened for teachers. A national counterterrorism strategy names pro-trans groups as a target. Division law requires school staff to out LGBTQ students to parents. Trans candidates were disqualified in 2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several national orders are enjoined. The counterterrorism strategy disclaims targeting people who disagree.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Institutional hostility is framed in state and federal policy; visitors may encounter it through school, election or outing channels.

minors_guardians.exposure: A travelling minor may face school facility designation and mandated outing to parents at school. A guardian may face school-level disclosure or exclusion. Care restrictions may apply to a minor's treatment.
minors_guardians.protection: Parental opt-out applies to curriculum material only. No documented guardian protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor-focused school rules and national prosecution threats for facilitators raise risk for families travelling with children.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific street-violence rate is documented. National hate-crime law exists, but only 23 states cover gender identity in bias-violence statutes, and this division is not confirmed as one of them.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute, national employment protection, and 33 local ordinances covering employment, housing and public accommodation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local protections do not reach visitors in unprotected jurisdictions, but federal hate-crime law applies.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and document challenges are unresolved. Marker-matching rules are announced, but the final text is unsourced. County-level refusal of birth-certificate corrections continues. Care and sports bills have unclear enforceability.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Marriage recognised regardless of sex, and a national employment ruling. Courts have blocked several national orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Frequent litigation swings mean the operative rule must be checked on the date of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Anchor 0.35-A is an exclusion register with refusals for visibly trans travellers, but no custody harm. This case is similar in document-based exclusion. It is higher because it documents no sexual abuse in custody and no national custody practice, and the entry risk is an open fraud route rather than a universal register.

Anchor 0.45-A has biometric document checks, detention and denial of care, and is close in universal exposure. This case is similar, but documented immigration custody sexual abuse and forced labour are more severe, so it is slightly lower. Division protections such as marriage recognition and employment law are partly offsetting.

Anchor 0.25-C has birth-sex housing, cross-dressing arrests and solitary confinement. This case has no documented housing-by-birth-sex rule for visitors, and facility law has no enforcement. This case is higher, though custody harms are comparable.

parsed.synthesis: The national document regime and documented immigration custody harms form the main operative exposure, reaching any visitor who is checked at the border or detained. The division's school facility designation and outing duty add exposure mainly for minors, with no documented enforcement. Official hostility and litigation uncertainty reduce predictability. Mitigations are real but partial: national hate-crime and employment law, marriage recognition, and local ordinances. Since no criminal penalty for identity-based presence is documented in the division, the rating sits in the Elevated band, lower than the 0.45 anchors because of documented custody sexual abuse and document refusals.
